title: Adaptive latency tiling dashboard for model+route with streaming vs non-streaming overlays
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description: Build a single, adaptive dashboard that tiles model x route cells showing p50/p95/p99 latency and error rates with an explicit streaming vs non-streaming toggle. The dashboard should: 1) surface cells that exceed SLO thresholds by visually expanding "hot" tiles, 2) link each tile to trace hooks and recent traces for that model+route+io_mode, 3) work with histogram/t-digest metrics to display percentile trends without exploding cardinality, and 4) be performant in Grafana for up to 500 model+route combinations. This ticket covers the dashboard UI, minimal metric pipeline changes to support the view, and tracing link integration. Implementation must avoid adding high-cardinality labels to the primary metrics stream; prefer computed rollups or pre-aggregated t-digests released to the observability cluster.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows a grid of tiles with rows=top N models (configurable) and columns=routes; each tile displays p50/p95/p99 latency and error rate for streaming and non-streaming modes.
Tiles that breach configured SLOs (per-tenant or global) are visually emphasized and can be filtered to show only breaches.
Clicking a tile opens a panel with the last 50 traces (via trace hooks) filtered to the selected model/route/io_mode and time window.
Backend metric footprint: no new high-cardinality time series created in the raw metrics pipeline; percentile data should be sourced from pre-aggregated t-digest snapshots or rollups.
Grafana dashboard performance: initial load < 3s for default N=30 models; interactions (filter/change mode) < 1.5s.
Documentation (Confluence) and playbook for SRE/Support on how to interpret tiles and run next-step diagnostics are linked from the dashboard.

2026-02-20 - Marcus Li: Spike complete. t-digest maintains ~1-2% p99 error vs full raw traces at 95th percentile of traffic; recommends using t-digest snapshots every 1m with 5s max staleness for dashboard freshness. Details in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/latency-tiling-spike

2026-02-25 - Marcus Li: Implemented initial rollup job prototype in infra repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2391 — writes to metrics-rollup.tdigests namespace. Observability team to validate retention/cost implications.

2026-03-02 - Design review (Heather Kim): provided two layout options — grid-first (compact tiles) and focus-first (one large tile with minitiles). We prefer grid-first for ops use. Design file: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DesignFile

2026-03-05 - Marcus Li: Added trace link integration; clicking tile generates a pre-filtered trace query that includes model, route, and io_mode. Sample traces endpoint: https://traces.internal.redwood.ai/search?service=inference&model={{MODEL}}&route={{ROUTE}}&io_mode={{IO_MODE}}

2026-03-09 - QA (Samir Patel): smoke tests show initial load at N=30 models = 2.8s; N=200 spikes to 5.3s. Created PR for dashboard optimizations: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1187
2026-03-10 - Ava Rodriguez: Merged spike docs and updated acceptance criteria to require performance targets. Planning rollout: beta to SRE + 3 customer AEs, then broader release.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: sampling frequency vs storage cost; decided on 1m t-digest snapshot with configurable retention per-tenant.
Fallback plan: if rollup job is delayed, dashboard will default to coarse percentiles computed from existing metrics (p50/p95 only) and gray-out p99 until rollups are available.
Future work: add ability to overlay model-quantization and hardware class (gpu/cpu) to explain latency variance.
